VST.summary: On Sep 29 the federal regulator (FERC) approved most of PJM's emergency capacity purchase but put it on hold until Feb 28, 2027 because of who pays, so the auction we expected to run Sep 30 to Oct 21 has been pulled with no new date. That moves one of our dated catalysts but does not change Vistra's earnings or contracts. Vistra also confirmed its Q3 call for Nov 6, one day after the date we had estimated.
VST.fair_value_reasoning: Fair value is 9.0x ~$8.15B forward EBITDA less ~$23.5B net debt and preferred, over 337M shares (~$151). The backstop procurement was rated 'low' magnitude with direction '?' in the memo and contributes nothing to that EBITDA: it buys new capacity for 2028/29, and Vistra's Meta (2.6 GW) and AWS (1.2 GW) contracts are bilateral and unaffected. FERC accepted the $555/MW-day cap and seller rules and objected only to cost allocation, transmission-owner exit rules and buyer collateral. So the change to cash flows is about 0%. The one open risk is that PJM had warned a change to the backstop could force it to delay the Dec 2029/30 Base Residual Auction. That would move a timing catalyst, not NTM EBITDA, and it is not confirmed yet. Sources: Utility Dive 2026-09-30, RTO Insider 2026-09-30, mgrid 2026-09-29.
VST.breaks: Catalyst 'PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement bid window 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-21 (results by 2026-12-02)' is postponed, with FERC suspending the procurement to 2027-02-28 and no new PJM date. FERC's chair called the cost allocation 'deeply flawed', which partly lights the memo's 'PJM political intervention' signpost (backstop design that caps East capacity value), though the $555 cap was accepted. Watch whether the mid-Dec 2029/30 BRA catalyst slips. The Q3 call is now company-confirmed for Nov 6 instead of the estimated Nov 5.

items.headline: Google and DOJ file jointly proposed Final Judgment in the ad-tech case (docket no. 1861, entered Oct 2, filed about 10:15pm ET); 41 pages, agreed core behavioural remedies (AdX-Prebid interoperability, no first/last look, Google Ads not bidding directly into DFP, separate DFP/AdX contracts, publisher data export), six-year monitor; disputes left for Judge Brinkema on timelines (AdX-Prebid 6 vs 12 months; global rollout day one vs +24 months) and monitor nomination/access; Google expected to appeal
items.why: This is the memo's dated catalyst (the Oct 2 joint final judgment). The filing is confirmed on the court docket (CourtListener, E.D. Va. 1:23-cv-00108, entry 1861 'Parties' Jointly Proposed Final Judgment', entered 10/02/2026: https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/66753787/united-states-v-google-llc/) and by MLex (https://www.mlex.com/mlex/technology/articles/2533905). It is the behavioural-only outcome the research already assumed after the Sept 2 ruling; the open disputes are about implementation speed and oversight, with no financial terms. The judge still has to sign it, then a 60-day implementation clock starts. Contents are from AdExchanger's Oct 5 report and were not checked against the 41-page PDF itself.

items.headline: Poland's UOKiK charges Alphabet, Google LLC, Google Ireland and Google Poland with possible abuse of dominance in compensation talks with Polish press publishers (rates offered without required data on use and revenue); maximum penalty up to 10% of turnover; proceedings ongoing
items.why: A new regulatory case, but an early-stage national one about publisher payments. The 10% cap is a legal maximum, not an expected fine (Polish fines are usually tied to Polish turnover and far smaller). It fits within the EU/regulatory risk the agents already carry and does not touch Search, Cloud or the DC Circuit appeal. Covered the same day by Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/alphabet-won-washington-got-charged-144229447.html (GOOGL about $345, +0.4%, Monday morning).

VST.summary: The US Energy Department officially offered Vistra a $4.2 billion loan on Oct 5 to pay for adding 433 MW to its Perry, Davis-Besse and Beaver Valley nuclear plants. This is an offer with conditions, not a signed loan, and the rate and term were not disclosed. It lowers the cost of upgrades that were already in our research (the Meta contracts), so it is worth roughly +1% to fair value, which is too small to change tonight's levels. The stock closed up 3.5% at $144.94, not the 6%+ some reports claimed.

items.headline: Energy Department Announces $4.2 Billion Investment to Boost Nuclear Power and Help Lower Energy Costs in Pennsylvania and Ohio (conditional loan commitment to Vistra)
items.why: Official DOE release (Office of Energy Dominance Financing, announced by Sec. Wright at Perry). Terms from the primary source: $4.2B CONDITIONAL commitment; 433 MW total uprates at Perry, Davis-Besse and Beaver Valley (per-plant MW not given in the release; the Jan 2026 Meta PPA split was 213/80/140 MW); preserves ~4 GW of existing baseload; includes an option to finance possible future Comanche Peak uprates. The interest rate, tenor and total project cost are NOT disclosed, and Vistra must meet technical, legal, environmental and financial conditions before definitive documents and funding. The research did not include the loan, but the 433 MW of uprates, their 2026-2034 capex (<20% by end-2028) and the Meta PPA revenue were already in the agents' cash flows. The loan only cuts the cost of funding them. Rough value: if DOE lends near Treasury + a small spread (~4.3-4.5%) versus Vistra's ~5.75-6.25% secured cost (its ~$4B of notes priced in April), saving ~1.5 pts on $4.2B drawn over ~2027-2034 gives ~$60M/yr pre-tax (~$47M after tax) once fully drawn. Discounted, that is ~$0.4-0.6B, or ~$1.2-1.8 per share on ~335M shares, about +0.8-1.1% of the ~$157 fair value. Net debt is unchanged, because the loan replaces market debt for capex that was already planned. That is within the agents' range, so the item is minor. The Comanche Peak option is upside, but it is speculative and has no terms.

items.headline: Illinois Governor's office: bipartisan PJM governors sign an MOU formally establishing the PJM Governors' Collaborative at the 2026 Governors' Summit on the State of PJM (Chicago)
items.why: Opened at the primary source. The release went out around 11:06am CT, after the 9:00am CT opening remarks (https://gov-pritzker-newsroom.prezly.com/daily-public-schedule-thursday-october-8-2026). It turns the 11-state group into a formal forum to develop joint positions, share technical help and coordinate with PJM, FERC and state regulators. It contains nothing on capacity price caps or the collar, caps on existing generation, auction design or generator revenues, so no cash-flow input moves. It does make the research's named risk of PJM political intervention (thesis-break list; memo risk 4) more organized. The group's agenda since 2025 includes a 'bifurcated auction' that would cap prices for existing plants (https://www.publicpower.org/periodical/article/governors-pjm-interconnection-launch-collaborative-act-various-issues), which would hit Vistra's PJM nuclear and gas fleet, but nothing like that was announced today. Watch for a joint filing at FERC. Unconfirmed: whether this MOU was the agenda's 4:30pm CT 'special announcement'. The release came out before that slot, and as of the evening of 10-08 no source tying the two together, and no other later announcement, could be found.

items.headline: Pre-summit coverage: governors to meet in Chicago Oct 8 after PJM members kept veto over governance reforms; agenda closes with a 4:30pm 'special announcement'

BKNG.summary: Nothing new and material on Oct 8-9. Booking filed nothing with the SEC and issued no press release. Agoda's deadline to fix its contracts with French hotels passed today, but neither the French regulator nor Booking has said whether it complied, and the most it could be fined is EUR 5.1M, which is too small to matter. Two items dated Oct 7, just before this window, should be checked if the last refresh missed them: Reuters reported that the FTC is preparing action against Priceline, with one source putting possible penalties above $500M (about 0.3% of fair value; the FTC risk was already in the research), and Wells Fargo cut its target to $190.

items.headline: Agoda's DGCCRF compliance deadline (contracts with French hoteliers) falls today; no outcome published by the DGCCRF or Booking Holdings
items.why: The DGCCRF communique (a copy hosted by the GHR hotel group, confirmed by GHR's May 12 article) says the DRIEETS Ile-de-France ordered Agoda Company Pte. Ltd on Mar 31, 2026 to bring its contract clauses and practices into line with EU P2B Regulation 2019/1150 and the Commercial Code by Oct 9, 2026, with periodic penalties of up to EUR 5.1M in total. The deadline and cap are verified. Whether Agoda complied is unknown: the DGCCRF site returned 403, and the PR feed, EDGAR and searches show no statement. Even the full EUR 5.1M (~$6M) is under 0.1% of the ~$5.4B annual net income. Booking.com amended its terms after the same kind of 2025 injunction, so a contract rewrite is the likely result. This does not touch the research's legal tail (FTC, Dutch claims, German suits, CNMC).

items.headline: Republications of Reuters' Oct 7 exclusive 'Priceline to face FTC action over deceptive hotel ads, sources say' (Insurance Journal, NWA Democrat-Gazette)

It reports, from anonymous sources, that the FTC is preparing action over ads that route users to the Guest Reservations affiliate site. One source put possible penalties above $500M; this figure is unverified. Booking had already disclosed the FTC matter in its Q2 10-Q, which the research covers. As of Oct 9, ftc.gov shows no complaint against Priceline. Even at $500M, the hit is about $0.67/share, or ~0.35% of the $191 fair value.

NFLX.summary: Netflix itself announced and filed nothing. Reuters, citing Puck News, reported on Friday that Netflix plans to cut about 5% of its staff (roughly 800 jobs) as soon as next week. Netflix declined to comment, so it stays unconfirmed. If it is confirmed, it would be a small plus for margins that fits the research's cost scenarios, not a thesis change. The stock closed near $72 on Friday, well above the $49 thesis-break level.

items.headline: Netflix plans to cut about 5% of its workforce, with an announcement possible next week (Reuters, citing Puck News; Netflix declined to comment)
items.why: This is a Reuters wire story (Harshita Mary Varghese, Bengaluru) republished by a radio station's site. Reuters only relays Puck's anonymous sources, so no second independent outlet confirms it, Netflix has made no filing or statement, and it counts as unverified. If it is confirmed, the size is small. About 800 roles at roughly $0.3B a year of fully loaded cost comes to about $0.23B after tax, or ~$0.06 per share, which is ~1.5% of FY27 EPS of ~$3.84 and ~+1% to fair value before one-off severance. That supports the January 2027 margin guide rather than breaking anything. Expect detail at Q3 results on Oct 20. Original relay: https://www.netflixjunkie.com/netflix-news-netflix-reportedly-set-to-restructure-and-trim-global-workforce-by-five-per-cent/ (it says ~850 of ~17,000).

items.headline: Netflix to cut about 6% of its workforce, roughly 1,000 jobs, mostly in product, technology, legal and HR; co-CEO memo says the company 'remains on track to deliver our full-year forecast'
items.why: Verified: Reuters (via Investing.com, Oct 14), AP (https://abcnews.com/Business/wireStory/netflix-laying-off-6-workforce-biggest-round-job-137262053) and NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/business/media/netflix-layoffs-rcna603454), which saw the memo, agree on ~6%, ~1,000 jobs and the affected teams; WSJ reported it first. Puck had already reported an ~850-job cut on Oct 9. No 8-K has been filed, and no charge or savings figure is disclosed. Rough scale: at about $250-300k per role, the yearly savings are ~$0.25-0.3B, which is ~0.5 point of margin or ~$0.05/share after tax. That is inside the agents' 1-2 point 2027 margin-expansion scenarios. The memo reaffirms the full-year forecast, so it is not a guidance change. Watch the Oct 20 report for a severance charge, likely in Q4 since Q3 ended Sep 30, and whether management frames it as margin support for 2027.

NFLX.summary: On Oct 15 Netflix said its content chief, Bela Bajaria, is leaving after almost 10 years. Former Disney TV chairman Peter Rice replaces her from Oct 26. The news came a day after about 1,000 job cuts, and several brokers trimmed their price targets ahead of results. The shares fell 2.9% on Friday to $70.54, about 44% above the $49 thesis-break level. Neither the leadership change nor the target cuts changes the forecast or the research numbers. The Q3 report is confirmed for Tuesday Oct 20 after the market close and remains the real test.

items.headline: Netflix names Peter Rice (ex-Chairman of Walt Disney Television) Chief Content Officer effective Oct 26; Bela Bajaria leaves after nearly 10 years
items.why: Verified against the Netflix newsroom release (Oct 15), CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/15/netflix-bela-bajaria-peter-rice.html) and Variety (https://variety.com/2026/film/news/netflix-bela-bajaria-leaving-layoffs-1236913504/). The person leaving is the head of the ~$17B content budget, not the CEO. The co-CEOs stay, and the release has no budget, spending or guidance figures. No 8-K is on EDGAR. This hits no memo trigger or research input: no guidance change, no deal, no catalyst date moved. It does bear on the main open question, content payments running at ~1.16x amortization (the agents assume ~1.12-1.15x). A new content chief could reset slate spending either way, and Wedbush reads it as a shift toward more focused content spend. Nothing is quantifiable yet. Watch for comments on the Oct 20 call and in the January 2027 guide.

items.headline: Brokers trim targets before Q3: BMO $135 to $125 (Outperform, cites slowing US/Canada growth, weak engagement, the CCO change); Wedbush $105 to $90 (Outperform, calls the CCO change a positive); Rosenblatt holds Neutral $75 and estimates ~$500M of layoff savings
items.why: BMO: Investing.com, Oct 16. Wedbush: Stocktwits News, Oct 16 (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/netflix-nflx-stock-price-target-cut-content-chief-change/cZxK2FgRBs1). Rosenblatt: Investing.com, Oct 16 (https://ng.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/rosenblatt-maintains-neutral-on-netflix-stock-amid-layoffs-exec-change-93CH-2740473). The 'verified' flag covers only that these notes were published, each from a single report. Their targets of $75-125 sit around and above the $76 fair value and carry no new company facts. Rosenblatt's ~$500M savings figure ($500k per role x ~1,000 roles, ~3% of 2026 operating profit) is a broker estimate, not a company figure. After tax it is ~$0.10/share, about 1 margin point, inside the agents' 1-2 point 2027 margin scenarios. Jefferies initiating at Buy with an $85 target is now repeated by Investing.com via Rosenblatt's note, but it remains undated. An aggregator's claim of a Barclays cut from $80 to $70 could not be confirmed or dated and is not counted.

NVDA.summary: No Nvidia-specific news changes the case: TSMC, which makes Nvidia's chips, beat its own forecast and guided next quarter well above it, which supports our demand view, while the stock fell to $214.13 on worries about how AI data centers are being financed (CoreWeave, a customer Nvidia has invested in, is under debt stress) and a hot producer-price report. The price is now around the memo's ~$215 add level and well above the $174.61 stop; the real tests are still the late-October hyperscaler capex guides and the ~Nov 17-18 results.

items.headline: TSMC Q3 2026: revenue $46.72B, above its $44.6-45.8B guide; Q4 guide $52.3-54.3B, gross margin 65-67%; CEO says leading-edge demand is 'extremely robust'; 2026 capex budget $60-64B reiterated
items.why: This is the memo's first dated catalyst (Oct 15). The Q4 guide midpoint ($53.3B) is ~18% above the Q3 guide midpoint and ~14% above Q3 actual, and HPC rose 22% q/q to 68% of revenue (per Market Business News). It supports the supply-constrained FY28 ~+70% view, but it is a read-through, not a change to Nvidia's cash flows, so it stays inside the agents' base case. Figures were taken from TSMC's IR page and match Market Business News and Yahoo Finance.

items.headline: Reuters: CoreWeave's slump puts spotlight on debt behind AI boom (~$50B debt, CDS ~1,000bp implying ~63% five-year default odds, 2031 bonds yield >16%)
items.why: Nvidia is a major CoreWeave investor and has agreed to buy its unsold capacity through April 2032 (per Reuters). This hits the memo's vendor-financing risk (Nvidia's stakes in AI customers, the $105B guarantee, DSO) and the bear case's debt-funded capex signpost. There is no default and Nvidia disclosed no loss, so the risk sits inside the agents' scenarios. The 'record 1,194.5bp' CDS figure from other outlets traces to ICE data relayed by aggregators and was not checked; Yahoo Finance's live blog independently reports the record move.

NFLX.summary: Netflix reported Q3 after the close today: revenue $12.87B (in line), operating margin 34.6% and EPS $0.87 (beat the $0.82 guide, mostly because costs landed earlier than planned), but the Q4 guide is weak (EPS $0.67, margin 26.0%), the 2026 free cash flow guide was cut from about $12.5B to about $12.0B and the 2026 ad revenue forecast was cut from about $3B to about $2.7B. The stock fell roughly 5-6% after hours to about $64.6, just under its 52-week low of $65.08; my best guess is the research fair value (about $76) moves down about 2%.
NFLX.fair_value_reasoning: Baseline: supervisor fair value $76 (60% ~18x NTM EPS ~$4.25, 40% equity FCF method on ~$13.6B NTM FCF at 4.4%). Note the pitch memo still quotes $80, the supervisor file says $76; I use $76. (1) 2026 earnings are roughly unchanged: Q3 EPS beat +$0.05 vs the $0.82 guide is largely expense timing that reverses into Q4; Q4 EPS guide $0.67 is $0.06 below the $0.73 consensus reported by TipRanks (single outlet, consensus figure not verified), so full-year EPS is about -$0.01 vs expectations. FY26 revenue $51.1B is 0.2% below the mid-point of the old range, FY26 margin 31.5% unchanged (includes ~30bp from headcount cuts). (2) FY27 EPS: ad revenue $2.7B vs $3B is about -$0.3B revenue; if 2027 ad revenue is also ~$0.3B lower at ~80% incremental margin that is ~$0.24B pre-tax, ~$0.05/share after tax, about -1.3% of ~$3.8-4.0 FY27 EPS. The ~1,000-person cut (Netflix quantifies only the Q4 cost, ~120bp of Q4 margin) offsets part or all of that in 2027 but the CFO declined to quantify 2027 savings, so I net FY27 EPS at about -0.5%. (3) Multiple: the research said the multiple, not the earnings, was the open question. A slowest-in-three-years revenue growth print, an ad shortfall and a below-consensus Q4 guide argue for about 0.5x lower on 18x, about -2.8% on the P/E leg (60% weight, about -1.7% of total). (4) FCF leg (40% weight): the $0.5B guide cut is attributed 'primarily' to a Q4 real estate transaction, which I treat as non-core, so core ~$11B base is unchanged; but 9-month content additions of $14.93B vs amortization $12.76B (1.17x) and Q3 alone 1.22x have not eased toward the ~1.1x full-year target, so I trim the leg by about 1% (-0.4% of total). Faster buybacks (record $4.8B, 63.9M shares in Q3, $22.3B authorization left) are a small plus, about +0.3% of total. Sum: about -0.4 -1.7 -0.4 +0.3 = about -2.2%, rounded to -2% (about $74.5); plausible range -4% to 0%. The after-hours price (~$64.6) is about 15% below the $76 fair value, so the move is larger than my fair value change. Sources: Netflix Q3 2026 letter (SEC ex-99.1), TipRanks, Investing.com.

items.why: Reuters (two anonymous sources; original page https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/bytedance-alibaba-tencent-place-over-35-billion-worth-nvidia-chip-orders-2026-10-20/ could not be opened here, so the report is read through TNW, Yahoo Finance and 247WallSt, all relaying the same Reuters story; TNW states it has not verified it) says 3M+ RTX PRO 5500 workstation cards (~$11,400 each, $35B+ at list) were ordered, 6M+ across China, Nvidia can build at most 3M worldwide in 2027, partners may get only 5-10%, samples December, shipments Q1 2027. Nvidia did not confirm the orders; its only on-record comment was about export rules. It is a workstation card, not a data-center chip, and the Q3 guide of $108B excludes China data-center compute. Arithmetic: 5-10% of 3M cards x $11,400 = about $1.7-3.4B, under 0.5% of the research FY28 revenue (~$650-690B), so possible small upside outside the agents' zero-China base, not a thesis input. NVDA.summary: No Nvidia filing, guidance change or deal that breaks the research. Chip stocks fell sharply today after an equipment maker (Lam Research) said near-term supply limits held back its outlook, and Nvidia closed down 4.4% at 212.21 USD, about 11% below the research close but far above the 174.61 USD stop. Nvidia also unveiled a container-sized data-center design with no revenue figures, and the dates of the next big customer spending reports (Oct 28-29) are now confirmed.

items.headline: Lam Research Q1 FY27 results: revenue 8.22 billion USD, December-quarter guide 8.6 billion USD +/-0.4 billion; shares fell after hours
items.why: Read the 8-K exhibit: revenue 8.22B USD (+22% on the June quarter), guide midpoint 8.6B USD, no numeric supply statement in the release itself. The trigger for today's chip sell-off is the CFO's call remark, reported by Yahoo Finance, that the guide 'would have been a bit higher if not for some near-term supply chain constraints' (single secondary source for the quote, so that part is unverified). It is sector news about equipment supply, not an Nvidia fact; it supports the research's supply-cap view (FY28 about 700-750B USD) rather than a demand break. Not a memo trigger.

AMZN.summary: Anthropic made its S-1 public this morning (Nasdaq ticker ANT, no price range or share count yet); the reported terms fit what the research assumed: AWS compute minimum of USD 110B from May 2026 to April 2036 sits inside the roughly USD 496B backlog, and the IPO value talked about (USD 1.5-2T) matches the base and bull cases. Two things are not settled: Amazon's exact ownership percent (reports say a 12% limit applies only to converting the remaining USD 6.2B of Amazon notes, against the research's 19.5%) and the lock-up length. I could not open the S-1 itself (sec.gov blocked my request), so I cannot confirm either. Meta launched about USD 35B of stock sales to fund AI spending, which is sector sentiment and no change to AMZN cash flows, and the Oct 29 after-close print date is unchanged.

items.headline: Anthropic, PBC files its S-1 with the SEC (accepted 9:00 a.m. ET, accession 0001628280-26-067168); prior confidential drafts ended 2026-10-09
items.why: The IPO is the catalyst the research already assumes (base case Anthropic IPO at about USD 1.5T, bull USD 1.92T, bear USD 1.0T). Filing existence and time confirmed from the SEC submissions feed; the S-1 body itself (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026067168/anthropicpbc-sx1.htm) returned a block for my generic request and is more than 10 MB for the page reader, so every term below comes from press coverage of it, not from my own read.

items.headline: S-1 valuation and offering terms: price range and share count left blank; Nasdaq ticker ANT; last private price USD 589.0095 per Series H-1 preferred (about USD 58.90 per Class A share after the 10-to-1 conversion); listing talked about for mid/late November
items.why: No valuation is in the filing, so nothing yet moves the stake value. Press talk of USD 1.5-2T (Fortune, WSJ via Investing.com, Yahoo Finance) sits between the research base case (USD 1.5T) and bull case (USD 1.92T). Price-range amendment is the next number to check. Reporting on the price range, ticker and timing agrees across Stock Titan, Fortune and Yahoo Finance but I did not open the S-1.

items.headline: S-1: Amazon holds USD 6.2B of Anthropic notes (at 6/30/26) that convert at the IPO only until Amazon would hold 12% of the company, unless Amazon waives; Amazon and Google each expected above 5% after the IPO, non-voting, no board or observer seat
items.why: The research uses 19.5% ownership at a USD 1.5T IPO (17.6% after the Public Benefit Fund and primary shares; range 17-21%) and a USD 190.4B carrying value. The 12% figure is a conversion limit on the notes, not a disclosed ownership percent; CNBC's summary says the filing caps the stake at 12%, StockTitan and OfficeChai describe it as a limit on note conversion, so the reports differ on what it caps. I could not read the beneficial-ownership table, so I cannot size it: each 1 point of Anthropic ownership at USD 1.5T is about USD 15B before tax, about USD 11B after the 24% tax the research uses, or roughly USD 1.0 per AMZN share (about 0.4% of the USD 265.83 research target (12m)). If the cap really limited Amazon to 12% the stake would be well below the research, so this is the first thing to verify against the S-1 table; I leave the research target (12m) unchanged until it is read.

items.headline: S-1: Anthropic minimum compute commitment to Amazon of at least USD 110.0B from May 2026 to April 2036, owed regardless of usage; AWS Trainium named among its chips; total non-cancelable cloud lines about USD 430B and up to USD 750B of compute possible
items.why: The research already carries AWS backlog of about USD 496B at 6/30 with more than USD 100B of expansion each from OpenAI and Anthropic (10-Q), so a USD 110B ten-year AWS minimum is the same contract, not new backlog. The WSJ (via Investing.com), PPC Land, Stock Titan and Dealroom all give USD 110B for AWS. Open question I cannot size: Dealroom attributes to the risk factors that hyperscaler commitments could be curtailed, repriced or terminated, while Stock Titan and OfficeChai say owed regardless of usage; if any part were curtailable it bears on the AWS backlog and on the memo's thesis-break wording about an AI-lab commitment renegotiated. Revenue-share terms: AWS Marketplace is one of three hyperscaler channels carrying about 48% of Anthropic first-half revenue, recorded gross with the fee booked as expense; no AWS-specific split or related-party terms found.

items.headline: S-1 lock-up: staggered releases (days 27, 48, 62, 76 for some holders); holders above 0.5% of fully diluted shares released at the earlier of Q3 2027 results or day 365
items.why: The research prices a 0.5-year lock-up as a 10.37% discount (1 year: 14.36%). If Amazon is released only at day 365, the extra 4.0 points on about USD 205B of after-tax stake is about USD 8B, roughly USD 0.75 per share or 0.3% of the research target (12m), and earlier staged tranches could offset it. Amazon's own tranche schedule not found.

items.headline: S-1 financials: first-half 2026 revenue USD 16.3B, net loss USD 80.7B, first operating profit in Q2 (USD 974M); top two customers about 20% of revenue; founders hold a special share with 50.1% of votes
items.why: Fortune, WSJ (via Investing.com) and CNBC coverage agree on revenue and the loss. The loss is large mainly on non-cash marks, and a profitable-at-the-operating-line lab supports the AWS commitment. No effect on AMZN cash flows by itself; the concentration and the competitor-with-hyperscalers language are risks to the AWS customer-quality argument that I cannot size.

items.headline: Meta launches concurrent offerings: 250M depositary shares of Series A mandatory convertible preferred at USD 50 each (about USD 12.5B, plus 37.5M option) and USD 22.5B of Class A common via forward sale agreements (plus USD 3.375B option); proceeds for general corporate purposes
items.why: Filed 10:41-12:04 UTC on Oct 26 (S-3ASR, FWP, two 424B5, confirmed in the SEC submissions feed and the preliminary 424B5 text). Total about USD 35B, up to about USD 38.4B with options; Meta debt was USD 83.7B at 9/30. The filing does not tie the money to AI capex (it names general corporate purposes) but the Financial Times earlier reported it was to fund AI ambitions. It follows Alphabet's much larger equity raise. Read-across: the largest AI spenders are now raising equity, which can pressure AI-capex sentiment and the multiple on AMZN's debt-funded capex (the thesis break of USD 188 prices exactly that stress), and an earlier ZeroHedge item said analysts expect Amazon and Microsoft to consider the same. It is a customer-demand positive only in the sense that Meta keeps spending. No AMZN filing or announcement of its own raise; the EDGAR feed shows nothing new since Oct 6. Meta share reaction today not found.

GOOGL.summary: Anthropic made its IPO filing public this morning (EDGAR S-1, 9:00 ET). Reports from the filing put Anthropic's minimum, pay-regardless-of-use commitment to Google Cloud at about USD 114.5B through July 2033, close to the roughly USD 111B the research already used, and no price range or valuation is set yet, so the stake value the research assumed (USD 1.5T IPO) is neither confirmed nor broken. Meta also launched a USD 95B stock raise to fund AI spending, which is a sector-sentiment item; Alphabet itself has filed nothing new and still reports on Oct 28 after the close.

items.headline: Anthropic, PBC files its public Form S-1 with the SEC (accepted 13:00 UTC / 9:00 ET); proposed Nasdaq listing as ANT, price range and share count not yet set
items.why: First public, audited look at the Anthropic stake and the Cloud commitment. Filing and date confirmed on EDGAR (data.sec.gov submissions feed for Anthropic, PBC: S-1 filed 2026-10-26, after DRS/A amendments on Oct 9, Oct 1 and Sep 4) and in Anthropic's own release. The release gives no valuation or price range, so the IPO valuation the research assumed (USD 1.5T, stake about 11-12.5% fully diluted, est. cost USD 23.3B, est. after-tax, after-lock-up stake value USD 124.71B) can be neither confirmed nor broken today; the stake adjustment (+USD 51.21B, +USD 4.15 per share) depends on the range once it is set. The S-1 document on www.sec.gov refused automated requests and the full text exceeds the size our fetch tool allows, so the figures below come from press reports of the filing, not from our own reading of it.

items.headline: Anthropic S-1: at least USD 114.5B owed to Google Cloud from April 2026 to July 2033, payable regardless of actual usage (about 22% of Google Cloud's USD 514B backlog at Jun 30, a Yahoo Finance calculation); other non-cancelable deals: Amazon USD 110.0B, Broadcom USD 161.2B (TPU capacity), Microsoft USD 44.9B
items.why: Against the research: the base round used about USD 111B of press-reported draft figures for the Google Cloud commitment (a May report of USD 200B over five years is a different, larger number), so USD 114.5B is a minimum inside the range the agents already carried; it adds no backlog and no cash flow the research lacked. Not marked verified: Yahoo Finance and a second outlet (PPC Land, OfficeChai) agree on USD 114.5B and the July 2033 end date, but both relay the filing and neither quotes it, and we could not open the S-1 text; PPC Land notes the S-1's own commitment total is left blank. Horizon-neutral points we could not size: (a) concentration, since one customer is about a fifth of the backlog; (b) counterparty strength, since the same reports give Anthropic first-half 2026 revenue of USD 16.3B against a USD 80.7B net loss (mostly accounting charges) and USD 430B of non-cancelable commitments, so the Google Cloud cash flows through 2033 lean on Anthropic raising IPO money and growing into them; (c) the reported soft SpaceX-unit compute deal (up to about USD 121B, cancellable on 90 days notice from early 2027) is a competing claim on Anthropic's budget. Alphabet is also an investor, so the same IPO funds both the stake and the customer. Not sized: how much of the remaining Broadcom TPU commitment (USD 161.2B) flows to Google's TPU business versus Broadcom.

items.headline: Anthropic S-1 on Google's holding: Google and Amazon each expected to hold over 5% after conversion, non-voting Class N shares; Google put in about USD 10B (Series G-2, Mar 2026) and USD 10B (Series H, May 2026); exact percentage not found in what we could read
items.why: The two USD 10B purchases match the dilution path in the research (a USD 10B tranche at about a USD 350B valuation, then the USD 10B Series H milestone tranche), so the cost-basis and ownership assumptions (pre-IPO estimate 12.5%, 11.28% fully diluted at the IPO) are not contradicted. The principal-stockholders percentage and any carrying value for Google were not available in the reporting we could open (articles still quote the 2025 court-filing figure of about 14%, cap 15%), so a stake above or below 12.5% remains open. Each 1 percentage point of the stake at a USD 1.5T valuation is about USD 15B before haircuts, so this is worth re-checking against the S-1's ownership table once someone can read it.

items.headline: Meta launches up to USD 95B equity raise for AI spending: USD 35B underwritten now (USD 22.5B common, USD 12.5B mandatory convertible preferred), up to USD 60B at-the-market later; Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom reported to have expressed interest in up to USD 5B
items.why: Filings confirmed on EDGAR (Meta submissions feed, 2026-10-26: S-3ASR, FWP and two 424B5); size and structure agree across the Irish Times and the Reuters-based Global Banking and Finance report. Meta says it needs to raise hundreds of billions of dollars over several years, reports Q3 free cash flow of negative USD 2.12B and a 2026 capex guide of USD 135-145B. For Alphabet: a hyperscaler customer and peer is paying for AI capacity with new equity, which supports the idea that the AI build-out continues (supportive of Cloud demand) but also tells the market that spending is outrunning internal cash, the worry behind the Oct 22 selloff, and the research exit multiple uses a peer set that includes AI spenders. Meta shares were reported down about 1.4% in the morning (7% on Thursday after its print). No source said anything about Google Cloud demand. We could not size an effect on the peer multiple or on Alphabet's own capex financing; Alphabet is net cash, so its own funding is not in question.

NVDA.summary: Two big filings landed on Oct 26 and both touch NVIDIA's customer-financing story without breaking the research: Meta filed to raise about USD 35 billion in new stock (USD 22.5 billion of common shares plus USD 12.5 billion of convertible preferred), with NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom together signalling non-binding interest in up to USD 5.0 billion, and Anthropic's public S-1 shows about USD 206 billion of contracts to rent NVIDIA-GPU capacity through Nscale, Lambda and SpaceX alongside heavy Google TPU and Broadcom commitments. Nothing on export controls, China or NVIDIA's own filings turned up for Oct 23-26; the stock rose about 2.4% on the day, and the other big cloud companies' spending plans (Oct 27-30) and the Nov 18 report are still the next tests.

items.headline: Meta files prospectus supplement for USD 22.5B Class A common stock offering via forward sellers; NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom indicate non-binding interest in up to USD 5.0B
items.why: Opened the 424B5 (read the first 100,000 of 231,597 characters). USD 22.5B of Class A shares sold by Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs affiliates under forward sale agreements, plus a 30-day option for USD 3.375B more; Meta gets no cash up front and expects proceeds only when the forwards settle, on or before Nov 19, 2027; use of proceeds is stated as general corporate purposes, with no mention of GPUs, data centers or capex, so the filing does not itself tie the money to NVIDIA hardware. NVIDIA is named as one of three chip suppliers whose indications of interest total up to USD 5.0B on the same terms as other buyers; not binding. Why it matters: it confirms the equity route to fund hyperscaler spending (supports demand capacity, matches the memo signpost of capex funded outside free cash flow) but also adds a possible new NVIDIA-owns-customer-equity link on top of the USD 25B committed ecosystem equity, the extended receivable terms and the USD 105B lease-guarantee cap already in the research. NVIDIA's own share of the USD 5.0B is not stated, so the extra exposure is at most about USD 5B shared three ways, small against a roughly USD 5T market value; I could not size anything beyond that. It also does not break the memo's Big-4 2027 capex check, which still waits on Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon (Oct 27-30).

items.headline: Meta preliminary prospectus supplement for USD 12.5B Series A mandatory convertible preferred (250M depositary shares at USD 50; Nasdaq symbol METAM planned)
items.why: Opened the second 424B5 (first 100,000 of 460,248 characters): 250M depositary shares at USD 50 is about USD 12.5B before costs, plus an option for 37.5M more; converts to Class A around Aug 15, 2029; proceeds for general corporate purposes; the dividend rate and net proceeds are still blank in the draft. With the common offering that is about USD 35B of announced new equity-type capital (up to about USD 40.4B with both options), which is real cash for Meta's capex without new debt, so it lowers the chance of a Meta spending cut but also shows Meta's free cash flow (negative USD 2.12B in Q3 per earlier coverage) no longer covers its AI build. The Class C stock dividend (declared Oct 19, charter effective expected Jan 19, 2027) is the same program already in the Oct 23 research. Not seen in this document: any NVIDIA indication of interest (the truncated text may hold it).

items.headline: Anthropic public S-1: at least USD 475B of cloud compute purchases (up to about USD 750B with chip leases); NVIDIA-GPU capacity via Nscale (up to USD 44.6B to 2033), Lambda (USD 41.3B to 2034) and SpaceX (up to USD 120.5B through 2029)
items.why: I could not open the S-1 itself (the page exceeds the fetch size limit and sec.gov blocks automated tools), so this rests on agreeing secondary reports: The Motley Fool, PPC Land (https://ppc.land/amazon-google-and-microsoft-hold-269bn-of-anthropic-compute-contracts/) and Fortune (https://fortune.com/2026/10/26/anthropics-s-1-makes-clear-its-on-the-hook-for-billions-in-compute-its-customers-can-walk-at-any-time-2/, totals only) agree on the Nscale and Lambda figures; the Nscale amount also matches Nscale's own S-1 filed Sept 18 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002110365/000119312526395475/ck0002110365-20260918.htm, from search snippet). Nscale and Lambda are described as non-cancellable except in limited circumstances; the SpaceX deal can be cancelled on 90 days' notice. About USD 206B of GPU-capacity contracts is direct demand evidence for NVIDIA chips bought by these landlords (PPC Land: every one of those providers buys its chips from NVIDIA). The same filing shows large non-NVIDIA commitments (Broadcom about USD 161B in equipment leases, Google TPU capacity USD 125-150B for 2028-2031, Google Cloud at least USD 114.5B, Amazon at least USD 110B), which is the TPU/ASIC share shift the supervisor already built into the capture rate. Much of Anthropic's own revenue can be cut at short notice, so NVIDIA's indirect exposure to one customer's credit is a risk the memo already names under neocloud and lab financing. I found no NVIDIA guarantee of these contracts in the reports; I did not read the S-1 for any NVIDIA equity stake beyond the up to USD 10B investment announced Nov 2025 (PPC Land; primary release at https://www.anthropic.com/news/microsoft-nvidia-anthropic-announce-strategic-partnerships, seen only as a search result), so any new NVIDIA financing term in the S-1 is unverified.

items.headline: Applied Materials to Increase its Strategic Investment in BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi): accelerated share purchase to about 20%

Price and amount are NOT disclosed (verified gap). My size estimate, unverified: Besi market cap about 13.2B (MarketScreener table, currency not stated, taken as EUR); 11 points of that is roughly EUR 1.5B or about USD 1.7-1.9B at about 1.15 USD per EUR (the accelerated purchase may carry a premium). That is about USD 2.1-2.4 per AMAT share, roughly 0.6% of the USD 395.93 close, and at 4.2% forgone interest about USD 0.09 of EPS (about 0.4% of NTM EPS of about 22.8), partly offset by the stake's value and any Besi dividends. The cash is swapped for an asset, and the research already counts the existing equity stakes (USD 2.42B) in its USD 10.0 net cash, so this is not a break in the net cash or multiple inputs. Not in the agents' scenarios, so it is not noise. I rate it minor on cash flows at any date, not because it is late: it is a minority stake with no control, and Besi's hybrid-bonding and 3D-packaging tools are a strategic option for Applied in AI packaging. Cannot size: the price paid; the hybrid-bonding revenue or margin upside (the release gives none); the chance that a later step above 20% needs a bid (Dutch rule above 30%) and Chinese regulatory approval, as with the failed Kokusai deal in 2021 (Reuters via MarketScreener); Besi's own China exposure. items.headline: Anthropic S-1: non-cancellable cloud compute commitments across Amazon, Alphabet, SpaceXAI and Microsoft of at least USD 389.9B; Yahoo Finance reports totals of USD 430B (up to 637B) in one article and USD 475B (up to 750B) in another; up to USD 120.5B with SpaceXAI through 2029
items.why: Amazon's USD 110B AWS commitment (May 2026-Apr 2036, non-cancellable) was already public from the Sep 28-30 draft-prospectus reports (Yahoo, citing Reuters) and sits inside the research's backlog assumption. New is the S-1 language that Anthropic's customers can cut usage with little notice and that compute can sit underused while cash commitments continue, which raises the risk that Anthropic's ability to pay AWS weakens in later years, plus Anthropic spreading compute across Microsoft, Google/Broadcom, Fluidstack and SpaceXAI. Outlets disagree on the totals and none I could open gave Amazon's own share, so I cannot size the cash-flow effect on AWS cash flows in the years after the 12-month horizon (they still enter the horizon multiple) and do not claim a thesis-break trigger (renegotiated AI-lab commitment) has fired. items.headline: Modine 8-K (Item 5.02, filed after the close, event dates Oct 21-27): new Executive Severance Plan; CEO severance raised to 2x pay plus target bonus (3x within 24 months after a change in control); performance and restricted stock awards amended so that a change in control pays at the greater of target or trend performance, with no proration on a qualifying termination; 'good reason' widened (reporting to another officer of a successor, loss of officer title)
items.why: Read in full on EDGAR. The company says the changes align severance with current market standards after a compensation-consultant review. It is not a CEO exit, a deal announcement or a guidance change, so it is not a memo thesis-break trigger. Cash cost is a one-off in the low tens of millions of USD at most and only if a change in control and a qualifying termination both happen (not sized from the filing; salary and bonus levels were not checked), against an enterprise value near 7.5 billion USD. What I cannot size: enhanced change-in-control terms can make a takeover slightly dearer and can be the housekeeping a board does when it expects bid interest, but there is no evidence of any approach. A takeover premium at any date would be a catalyst outside the agents' scenarios; I cannot size its probability or price, so I leave the research target unchanged and flag it.

items.headline: Meta Platforms free writing prospectus: USD 22.5B Class A common stock plus USD 12.5B mandatory convertible preferred depositary shares, a planned USD 60B Class C at-the-market program from Q1 2027; Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom named as cornerstone investors with non-binding interest in up to USD 5.0B in aggregate of the common stock
items.why: Opened the SEC filing. Meta is funding its AI build-out with new equity, which supports the 2027 hyperscaler capex base the agents used (Meta 2027 consensus USD 185.6B of the USD 934.5B Big-4 total) but moves part of that funding from cash flow to external capital. Nvidia buying any of it is vendor financing of a customer, the same circular-financing theme as the USD 105B guarantee and extended-term receivables in the supervisor's break list. Nvidia's share is not stated and the whole three-company ceiling is USD 5.0B, small against FY27 H1 free cash flow of USD 69.9B. Not sized and not outside the scenarios: the USD 60B at-the-market program lands after the horizon (Q1 2027 onward), and whether capex funded by equity and preferred stays as high in 2028-29 as cash-funded capex would is a horizon-multiple question I cannot size from this filing.

items.headline: Q3 2026 results (after the close): EPS 2.12 vs about 3.02; Cloud revenue 30.71B (+103%), Cloud operating income 11.12B; capex 51.36B; FCF -9.07B; 2027 capex to 'increase significantly'; stock about -8 to -11% after hours
items.why: Cross-checked across Investing.com (slides and call transcript), TradingKey, Blockonomi and 9to5google, not at the primary source. Largest likely gaps against our research: free cash flow (trailing twelve months fell about 34B in the quarter per outlet figures), third-party compute and depreciation margin headwinds, 2027 capex (unsized; each 50B of extra annual outflow matters at any date), buyback path (none seen in H1; Q3 unverified), and the SpaceX stake mark (about 8B a quarter, unsized without the 10-Q). Cloud and backlog run ahead of our path. The post-print update is requested from the coordinator.

items.headline: Modine 8-K (Item 5.02): new Executive Severance Plan; CEO and equity-award change-in-control terms enhanced

items.headline: Meta pricing term sheet: common stock offering upsized to USD 25.0B (40M Class A shares at USD 625.00, forward sale, settlement on or before Nov 19, 2027); USD 12.5B of 6.50% Series A mandatory convertible preferred; planned USD 60B Class C at-the-market program from Q1 2027
items.why: Opened the free writing prospectus (pricing date Oct 26, trade date Oct 27, settlement Oct 29; filing timestamp not visible, so the in-window date is the trade date). Common size rose from USD 22.5B to USD 25.0B; preferred stays USD 12.5B at 6.50% with conversion to Aug 15, 2029; Meta last traded at USD 630.56 on Oct 26 and priced at USD 625.00. The document says a future USD 60B at-the-market program for Class C stock is not expected to start before Q1 2027 and no agreement exists. This was not in the Oct 26 research. It supports funding of hyperscaler capex outside free cash flow (inside the memo signpost and the capex-digestion scenarios) but also shows the largest buyers need outside capital. The pricing sheet does not mention NVIDIA, AMD or Broadcom, so NVIDIA's actual allocation within the non-binding USD 5.0B (Oct 26 424B5, already in the research) is unsized; if NVIDIA takes equity it adds to the customer-equity exposure already in the research (USD 25B ecosystem equity, extended receivables, USD 105B lease-guarantee cap). The USD 60B program lands after the 12-month horizon but is judged on cash flows at any date: it lengthens the funding runway for 2027-28 capex, direction positive for demand, size unquantified.

VST.summary: Nothing new from Vistra itself in the window: no filings, no company release and no PJM ruling that I could find. Two sector items are real but already inside the research: the US Energy Department's conditional loan of up to 5 billion USD to Constellation for nuclear uprates (Oct 27), and GE Vernova's strong results with record gas turbine demand (Oct 28). Their long-run effect on PJM capacity prices and on new gas supply could not be sized.

items.headline: Energy Department announces up to 5 billion USD conditional loan to Constellation for nuclear uprates (about 1.1 GW across 8 plants in PJM and MISO)
items.why: Confirmed by the DOE release and by Utility Dive (https://www.utilitydive.com/news/doe-loans-constellation-alliant-nuclear-gas/873011/). It is a conditional commitment, not funded. It is the same programme that offered Vistra up to 4.2 billion USD on Oct 5 (before the window, Utility Dive 2026-10-06), so it adds no Vistra cash flow. It adds cheap financing for a direct competitor and about 1.1 GW of future PJM and MISO supply. That is a small long-dated downward pressure on capacity prices after the 2029/30 collar, which the research already carries (PJM post-2030 cap probability 0.4, about -3 USD per share). The added supply and its effect on the 2030/31+ price are not sized.

items.headline: GE Vernova Q3 2026: orders 29.3 billion USD (+96% organic), gas power backlog plus slot reservations 122 GW, 2026 revenue and free cash flow guidance raised
items.why: Company 8-K release, read directly. The stock fell about 6% on the 9 billion USD Trench acquisition (24/7 Wall St, 2026-10-28), not on the operating numbers. The release does not mention Vistra or independent power producers. It shows strong new gas build demand and tight turbine supply, which supports the replacement-cost value of existing fleets, while a large wave of new gas plants from about 2029 is a later threat to merchant power and capacity prices. Not sized; no pricing or lead-time figures were given.

items.headline: Abbott receives FDA approval for first and only device in the U.S. to treat leaks after heart valve replacement without additional surgery (Amplatzer Paraclose PVL Occluder)
items.why: Real regulatory win in Structural Heart (single-arm PARADIGM study, 200 patients; leak affects 7-17% of mitral and 5-10% of aortic valve replacements), but the release gives no sales figure and the niche is small against a 12-month target built on Libre, electrophysiology and Exact Sciences drivers. It sits inside the 'Other Medical Devices' driver; no change to cash flows I can size.

items.headline: Abbott initiates pivotal trial for Cephea device, an innovative treatment for mitral heart valve disease (CROWN-MV, up to 585 patients)
items.why: Starts the pivotal study of an investigational device (not approved in the US), so any revenue is years past the horizon; it is not in the agents' numbers and I cannot size it from this release (no market or sales figures). Kept as minor, not none, because later cash flows count in the horizon multiple; the dated 30-day feasibility data at TCT on 2026-11-01 is the next checkpoint.

items.headline: KLA Sept-quarter results: revenue $4.14B (+29% y/y), Dec-quarter guide ~$4.7B; raises 2026 wafer-fab-equipment (WFE) estimate to mid-$150B (incl. advanced packaging) and expects 2027 above $200B; China 27-29% of its revenue, falling to low-20% in 2027

The research uses SEMI at $143.9B (2026), $175.3B (2027), $220B (2028); KLA's mid-$150B and >$200B are above that, but KLA's figure includes advanced packaging, so it is not like-for-like. Upside to AMAT 2027-28 revenue is therefore unsized here, and the bull scenario ($697) already covers a stronger WFE path. A supply-constraint and DRAM-cost caveat is in KLA's own commentary. Not verified: I opened the KLA 8-K cover (item 2.02, dated Oct 28, confirms the earnings release exists) but the exhibit text was not reachable, and the figures come from MarketBeat and its Yahoo syndication, which are one original, not two independent outlets. AMZN.summary: Amazon's Q3 report (Oct 29, after the close) missed on profit and sales by a hair (EPS $1.89 vs about $1.96-1.97 expected; sales $201.9B vs about $202.2-202.3B) but AWS grew 39% to $46.0B (beat, fastest in about five years) with $17.8B of operating profit; Q3 capex was $77.3B, full-year capex is still about $220B, and the Q4 guide is sales $240-247B and operating income $28.5-33.5B (midpoint $31.0B vs about $33.0B expected). The stock fell 4.3% in the regular session to $243.79 and a further 5-7% after hours (about $227-232), far above the $188 thesis-break price; I treat the print as material because of the lower profit guide and a much higher debt load than the research assumed, with a small negative best guess of about -1.5% on the 12-month target.
AMZN.fair_value_reasoning: Best guess -1.5% on the $266.70 research target (about -$4), wide error band (roughly -5% to +3%); every number below is my estimate unless tied to a source. (1) Q4 operating income guide: midpoint $31.0B vs about $32.99B expected (Yahoo live blog) = -$2.0B. Pre-tax $2.0B x 0.79 / 10.929B diluted shares (8-K) = $0.145 per share, or 1.2% of the research's horizon NTM EPS of $12.53 (supervisor.json). Q4 2026 is not itself in the horizon NTM window, so I count about half as a run-rate signal: about -0.6% on the P/E leg. (2) Net debt: the research's SOTP deducts $61.1B at Oct-2027 (consensus path; end-2026 consensus $22.3B). The 8-K shows long-term debt $173.1B vs cash and securities $114.2B at Sep 30 = at least $58.9B net already, with Q4 and all of 2027 capex still to come (TTM free cash flow -$42.4B; research notes 2027 capex consensus $277B and a standing view near $300B+). If 2027 free cash flow is -$50B to -$100B the horizon figure is plausibly $40-70B above $61.1B, i.e. $3.7-6.4 per share, 1.4-2.4% of $266.70; the SOTP leg has 42.5% weight, so about -0.6% to -1.0% on the target (the current-portion of debt and leases are not in the figure I used). (3) Peer multiples: the exit multiple is set from the peer median; GOOGL reportedly fell 12% on Oct 28 and AI names sold off Oct 29 (single-outlet claim, not verified), so the peer P/E may drop a little; unsized. (4) Offsetting upside I could not size: AWS revenue beat consensus by about 1-2% ($45.98B vs $45.29-45.68B), growth 39% with a 38.7% operating margin (17.773/45.984), and management reportedly said AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028 (one outlet, unverified); advertising ($19.6B vs about $20.8B expected) and online stores (+2%, vs about $69.6B expected) missed, which hits the ads and stores legs of the SOTP, also unsized. Net: -0.6% (guide) -0.8% (net debt) -0.3% (peers/ads/stores, a guess) +0.2% (AWS, a guess) = about -1.5%. No Anthropic mark: Q3 other income was -$703M vs +$10,186M a year earlier, so the research's $190-192B Anthropic carrying value is untouched by this quarter.
AMZN.breaks: Does not hit the thesis-break test (AWS growth falling to the low 20s, an AI-lab commitment renegotiated, or a 2027 capex guide far above about $300B with no AWS acceleration): AWS accelerated to 39% and 2026 capex was held at about $220B. It does hit two research inputs: the memo's catalyst of the Q3 print (Q4 operating-income guide below consensus, EPS and sales slightly below) and the SOTP horizon net-debt input ($61.1B at Oct-2027 looks too low given about $59B net debt already at Sep 30). No 2027 capex guide was in the release.

items.why: Opened at the primary source. Actuals (US$ millions): net sales 201,944 (+12%, 13% ex-FX); AWS 45,984 (+39%) with operating income 17,773 (vs 11,434; 38.7% margin); North America 112,852 (+6%) with OI 8,723; International 43,108 (+5%) with OI 1,580; total operating income 28,076 (13.9% margin); net income 20,685 (vs 21,185); diluted EPS $1.89 (vs $1.95) on 10,929M shares. The release gives no Q3 Anthropic gain (other income net was -$703M vs +$10,186M; the year-ago $9.5B Anthropic pre-tax gain explains the net-income decline). Capex (purchases of property and equipment) $77,259M vs $35.1B a year ago and $54.2B in Q2 per the research facts; 2026 cash capex still 'approximately $220 billion'; TTM operating cash flow $168.3B, TTM free cash flow -$42.4B. Balance sheet at Sep 30: cash $55.8B plus marketable securities $58.4B; long-term debt $173.1B (vs $65.6B at Dec 31, 2025). Q4 guide: sales $240.0-247.0B (+12-16%, includes about 60bp FX headwind, high-teens ad growth expected), operating income $28.5-33.5B (Q4 2025: $25.0B). Judgement: material. AWS acceleration supports the thesis (no thesis-break test is hit), but the Q4 profit guide is below consensus, EPS and sales were slightly below, and the debt build is much faster than the research's consensus net-debt path. Sized at about -1.5% on the target, see fair_value_reasoning; what I could not size is the AWS upside and the ads/stores shortfall on the SOTP legs.

NVDA.summary: Alphabet and Microsoft reported on Oct 28 and neither broke the research: Alphabet spent USD 51.4 billion in the quarter, kept 2026 at USD 195-205 billion and said 2027 will rise significantly (no dollar figure), while Microsoft's Azure grew 48% and its spending came in below forecast only because outside GPU-rental capacity arrived late. items.headline: Alphabet Q3: capex USD 51.4B, 2026 guide USD 195-205B unchanged, 2027 to 'increase significantly'; Cloud revenue USD 30.7B (+100%+), free cash flow negative USD 9.1B
items.why: Verified by two outlets that agree on the Q3 capex (USD 51.4B), the unchanged 2026 range and the negative USD 9.1B free cash flow: Fortune (opened) and the Motley Fool earnings-call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/29/alphabet-googl-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/, opened). I could not open Alphabet's own release (abc.xyz page held no release text; sec.gov is blocked to automated tools). Call detail from the transcript: Google Cloud backlog USD 561B (just over 55% to be recognised within 24 months); started renting third-party compute at the end of Q3 because supply is constrained (a positive for GPU-rental providers that buy NVIDIA chips); 'the latest NVIDIA GPUs' sit alongside TPUs, with nearly 100 customers on TPUs and TPU inventory up to USD 13.3B from USD 2.4B at year-end; USD 924B of maximum future purchase commitments. 2027: management gave no dollar figure ('increase significantly', detail on the Q4 call). Fortune's line that 2027 'is expected to rise to about USD 300 billion' conflicts with the transcript and with the Fool article, which calls USD 300B an analyst forecast, so I treat that number as unverified and do not use it. Against the research: the supervisor's Big-4 2027 consensus has Alphabet at USD 284.8B, i.e. roughly +40% on a ~USD 200B base, so 'significantly' is consistent with it and the capex check (USD 934.5B) is not broken, but it is also not confirmed until a number is given in Q4. The TPU share gain and externalisation is the ASIC-displacement risk the supervisor already carries in the capture rate. Unsized: the TPU hardware build (inventory and USD 924B commitments) is a lasting claim on the same capex budget; I cannot split it between TPU and NVIDIA GPUs from these sources.

items.headline: Alphabet shares down about 12.7% intraday on Oct 29 after the print; Search growth slowed to 12%, USD 8.7B paper loss on equity stakes, funded partly by equity and debt
items.why: Fool (opened) shows GOOGL down 12.74% at 2:55 PM ET on Oct 29 (an intraday snapshot, no close) and NVDA down 1.2% in the same page ticker; Fortune (opened) gives the after-hours fall (more than 11%), Search +12% (vs 17% in Q2 and 19% in Q1, analysts expected 15%) and the USD 8.7B paper loss on equity investments. Financing facts: Fool says Alphabet sold USD 12.4B of stock and raised USD 28.7B of new debt in the quarter; Fortune says it raised USD 84.8B of equity in June (including USD 10B from Berkshire Hathaway); long-term debt USD 125.1B per the transcript. Why it matters: the selloff is mostly about Search and accounting, but it shows the market punishing a hyperscaler whose free cash flow no longer covers its AI spending. That fits the memo's tail (capex funded outside free cash flow, then a digestion cut) and the Oct 26 Meta equity raise already in the research; nothing here cuts a Big-4 capex number yet. NVDA's own move is small (-1.2%). Unsized: a lasting financing squeeze at several hyperscalers would show up in 2028+ capex, not in 2027 guides.

items.headline: Microsoft FY27 Q1: revenue USD 92.3B, Azure +48% (USD 33.2B, guide +49-50%), capex USD 45.2B vs about USD 50.7B expected, Q2 capex 'over USD 50B'
items.why: Microsoft's own release (opened) confirms revenue USD 92.3B, Azure +48% to USD 33.2B, Microsoft Cloud USD 63.9B (+30%) and cash additions to property and equipment of USD 39.4B; it states no capex guidance. The call figures come from the Tradingkey call transcript (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262249601-tradingkey), Stock Titan (https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/microsoft-q1-fiscal-2027-earnings-azure-growth-ai-spending) and Explainx (https://explainx.ai/blog/microsoft-170-billion-calendar-2027-capex-guidance-azure-48-percent-what-it-means-2026), which agree: capex and finance leases USD 45.2B (below the roughly USD 50.7B StreetAccount estimate because third-party capacity deliveries, mostly from GPU-as-a-service providers, were delayed), about three-quarters on short-lived assets (CPUs and GPUs), Q2 'over USD 50 billion', H2 FY27 spend to accelerate and third-party deliveries shifted into H2, 'customer demand continues to exceed available supply', free cash flow USD 18.6B and still positive in FY27, commercial backlog (RPO) USD 677B. The 'USD 170 billion' figure is not verified, see the next item. Why it matters: a timing slip of GPU rental capacity, not a cut; demand is stronger than the 45% Azure forecast; capex is pushed into H2 rather than lost. Slightly positive read-across for NVIDIA neocloud and Microsoft GPU demand, and inside the supervisor's scenarios (Microsoft 2027 consensus USD 207.6B).

items.headline: Microsoft 'about USD 170 billion' capex-plus-finance-lease figure: reported as calendar 2027 (Tradingkey, Explainx citing CNBC) or fiscal 2027 (Investinglive headline); period unresolved
items.why: Unverified, so it cannot raise the day's verdict, but it is the number that matters most for the memo's Big-4 2027 capex check. Sources disagree on the year: Tradingkey's transcript summary and Explainx (citing CNBC) say calendar 2027; the Investinglive headline (https://investinglive.com/stocks/microsoft-sees-170bn-capex-in-fiscal-2027-but-says-it-will-stay-cash-flow-positive/, search result only, fetch failed) says fiscal 2027; Stock Titan says no FY27 or calendar 2027 figure was given. Arithmetic points against both labels: Q1 USD 45.2B plus Q2 'over USD 50B' plus an accelerating H2 puts fiscal 2027 well above USD 170B, and Microsoft's July guide for calendar 2026 was about USD 175B (Stock Titan), so USD 170B for calendar 2027 would be a decline, which sits badly with 'accelerate in H2' and with Microsoft's USD 207.6B 2027 consensus. A likely reading is a trim of calendar 2026 from USD 175B to about USD 170B because of the delayed third-party capacity (about a USD 5B gap, matching the Q1 shortfall), but I could not confirm that against the transcript or 10-Q. If it truly means calendar 2027, Microsoft alone would be about USD 38B (18%) below the USD 207.6B the supervisor used, which would be a material break of the Big-4 capex check (roughly -4% on the Big-4 total of USD 934.5B before any offsets from Alphabet); I have not sized the NVDA effect because the reading is unresolved. Needs the call transcript or the 10-Q at the next refresh.

items.headline: FCC adopts proposal (NPRM) to add 482 MHz (5 to 13 bands) for satellite-to-phone service; drops requirement to lease from every co-channel carrier; opens comment period, grants SpaceX no spectrum
items.why: This is the dated Oct-29 catalyst in the memo and it landed as a proposal only (comments due 60 days after Federal Register publication, final rules later), so no cash-flow change inside the agents' scenarios. Unverified: I found no FCC release or reputable outlet (a second blog, teslanorth, agrees but is also not reputable) and the adopted text was not yet public. Unsized and not set aside for being post-horizon: if the final rule keeps the relaxed leasing/coexistence route and keeps 3.45 GHz (AT&T's 2022 auction band), it lowers the barrier to a satellite fourth competitor in AT&T's own mid-band, which belongs in the horizon multiple/bear weight (agents already carry 0.35 probability of a national SpaceX carrier 2028-2031); I could not size it. Memo signpost 'carrier consent kept' is now looking weaker pending the adopted text.

items.headline: Same FCC proposal, as adopted: leasing from all co-channel licensees replaced by certified coexistence agreements or owning the ground license, license area limited to where service is provided
items.why: Second independent blog confirming the vote happened and the content of the leasing change; still not a primary or reputable source, so the day cannot be rated material on it. Final vote has no date.

T.summary: No AT&T-specific news in the window and no AT&T filings since 2026-10-21; the 2.2% rise (Verizon +3.8%) looks like a defensive rotation. The one dated event, the 2026-10-29 FCC vote, went as the research expected: a unanimous vote to seek comment on opening 482 MHz more spectrum to satellite-to-phone service, with the rule changes (including easing the need to lease from every carrier) still only a proposal, so we call it minor but could not size the final rule's bands, terms or timing, which could matter to cash flows after our horizon.

items.headline: FCC votes unanimously to seek comment on adding 482 MHz (five bands to 13) to satellite-to-phone rules; carriers could be bypassed via coexistence deals or satellite firms holding licenses; no date set for final rules
items.why: This is the 10-29 catalyst in the memo (direction negative, medium); the outcome is a proposal, not a final rule, and the FCC was receptive to the carriers' objection on the 2.5 and 3.45 GHz bands (adjusted how it seeks comment). Two trade outlets agree on the vote, but I did not open an FCC primary source, so the consent terms are unverified. Not sized: which bands survive, whether carrier consent is truly weakened, and the date of any final rule; a loosened consent rule would help a fourth entrant after our horizon, which belongs in the horizon multiple but cannot be sized from this proposal.

items.headline: Second report on the same FCC vote: proposal drops requirement to lease from every carrier on the same airwaves; carriers (via CTIA) had asked to remove 2.5 and 3.45 GHz (290 of the 482 MHz)
items.why: Corroborates the vote and the consent change; it does not say whether the carriers' two bands stayed in the approved text.

items.headline: FCC also advances an auction plan for 25 MHz (1675-1695 and 2020-2025 MHz) usable for phones, satellite-to-phone or both
items.why: Small block, early-stage proposal; no AT&T cash-flow effect we can identify. Who might bid, and when, is not sized.

AMZN.summary: Amazon's Q3 report (Oct 29, after the close) missed on profit and sales by a hair (EPS $1.89 vs about $1.96-1.97 expected; sales $201.9B vs about $202.2-202.3B) but AWS grew 39% to $46.0B (beat, fastest in about five years) with $17.8B of operating profit; Q3 capex was $77.3B, full-year capex is still about $220B, and the Q4 guide is sales $240-247B and operating income $28.5-33.5B (midpoint $31.0B vs about $33.0B expected). The stock fell 4.3% in the regular session to $243.79 and a further 5-7% after hours (about $227-232), far above the $188 thesis-break price; I treat the print as material because of the lower profit guide and a much higher debt load than the research assumed, with a small negative best guess of about -1.5% on the 12-month target.
AMZN.fair_value_reasoning: Best guess -1.5% on the $266.70 research target (about -$4), wide error band (roughly -5% to +3%); every number below is my estimate unless tied to a source. (1) Q4 operating income guide: midpoint $31.0B vs about $32.99B expected (Yahoo live blog) = -$2.0B. Pre-tax $2.0B x 0.79 / 10.929B diluted shares (8-K) = $0.145 per share, or 1.2% of the research's horizon NTM EPS of $12.53 (supervisor.json). Q4 2026 is not itself in the horizon NTM window, so I count about half as a run-rate signal: about -0.6% on the P/E leg. (2) Net debt: the research's SOTP deducts $61.1B at Oct-2027 (consensus path; end-2026 consensus $22.3B). The 8-K shows long-term debt $173.1B vs cash and securities $114.2B at Sep 30 = at least $58.9B net already, with Q4 and all of 2027 capex still to come (TTM free cash flow -$42.4B; research notes 2027 capex consensus $277B and a standing view near $300B+). If 2027 free cash flow is -$50B to -$100B the horizon figure is plausibly $40-70B above $61.1B, i.e. $3.7-6.4 per share, 1.4-2.4% of $266.70; the SOTP leg has 42.5% weight, so about -0.6% to -1.0% on the target (the current-portion of debt and leases are not in the figure I used). (3) Peer multiples: the exit multiple is set from the peer median; GOOGL reportedly fell 12% on Oct 28 and AI names sold off Oct 29 (single-outlet claim, not verified), so the peer P/E may drop a little; unsized. (4) Offsetting upside I could not size: AWS revenue beat consensus by about 1-2% ($45.98B vs $45.29-45.68B), growth 39% with a 38.7% operating margin (17.773/45.984), and management reportedly said AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028 (one outlet, unverified); advertising ($19.6B vs about $20.8B expected) and online stores (+2%, vs about $69.6B expected) missed, which hits the ads and stores legs of the SOTP, also unsized. Net: -0.6% (guide) -0.8% (net debt) -0.3% (peers/ads/stores, a guess) +0.2% (AWS, a guess) = about -1.5%. No Anthropic mark: Q3 other income was -$703M vs +$10,186M a year earlier, so the research's $190-192B Anthropic carrying value is untouched by this quarter.
AMZN.breaks: Does not hit the thesis-break test (AWS growth falling to the low 20s, an AI-lab commitment renegotiated, or a 2027 capex guide far above about $300B with no AWS acceleration): AWS accelerated to 39% and 2026 capex was held at about $220B. It does hit two research inputs: the memo's catalyst of the Q3 print (Q4 operating-income guide below consensus, EPS and sales slightly below) and the SOTP horizon net-debt input ($61.1B at Oct-2027 looks too low given about $59B net debt already at Sep 30). No 2027 capex guide was in the release.

items.headline: Amazon.com Announces Third Quarter Results (8-K Exhibit 99.1): sales $201.9B (+12%), AWS $46.0B (+39%), operating income $28.1B, EPS $1.89; Q4 guide sales $240-247B, operating income $28.5-33.5B
items.why: Opened at the primary source. Actuals (US$ millions): net sales 201,944 (+12%, 13% ex-FX); AWS 45,984 (+39%) with operating income 17,773 (vs 11,434; 38.7% margin); North America 112,852 (+6%) with OI 8,723; International 43,108 (+5%) with OI 1,580; total operating income 28,076 (13.9% margin); net income 20,685 (vs 21,185); diluted EPS $1.89 (vs $1.95) on 10,929M shares. The release gives no Q3 Anthropic gain (other income net was -$703M vs +$10,186M; the year-ago $9.5B Anthropic pre-tax gain explains the net-income decline). Capex (purchases of property and equipment) $77,259M vs $35.1B a year ago and $54.2B in Q2 per the research facts; 2026 cash capex still 'approximately $220 billion'; TTM operating cash flow $168.3B, TTM free cash flow -$42.4B. Balance sheet at Sep 30: cash $55.8B plus marketable securities $58.4B; long-term debt $173.1B (vs $65.6B at Dec 31, 2025). Q4 guide: sales $240.0-247.0B (+12-16%, includes about 60bp FX headwind, high-teens ad growth expected), operating income $28.5-33.5B (Q4 2025: $25.0B). Judgement: material. AWS acceleration supports the thesis (no thesis-break test is hit), but the Q4 profit guide is below consensus, EPS and sales were slightly below, and the debt build is much faster than the research's consensus net-debt path. Sized at about -1.5% on the target, see fair_value_reasoning; what I could not size is the AWS upside and the ads/stores shortfall on the SOTP legs.
